stories.headline: Sotomayor Says She Hopes Supreme Court Will Overturn Presidential Immunity Ruling
stories.summary:
Supreme Court Justice Sonia Sotomayor said Saturday that she hopes the court's decision granting former presidents broad criminal immunity will be overturned, saying her colleagues have done some "crazy things." She spoke at a civics education event at George Washington's Mount Vernon estate. It was the first time she had publicly commented on the matter in this way.

Asked how hopeful she is about the rule of law, Sotomayor said the country is going through a "rough patch," referring to the state of rule of law and civic discourse. The remarks drew coverage from more than two dozen outlets across the political spectrum, in part because of the political moment. Democrats won the Senate in Tuesday's midterm elections, which will make it harder for President Trump, who nominated three justices in his first term, to confirm a nominee if a vacancy arises.

Pressure has grown on conservative Justices Clarence Thomas and Samuel Alito to retire, though neither has shown any sign of imminently stepping down. Many conservatives view the loss of both chambers of Congress as a setback for their judicial ambitions, while some liberal commentators have urged older justices to act with their legacies in mind. Critics of Sotomayor's remarks may view public comments from a sitting justice on a decided case as unusual, while supporters see them as a candid defense of the rule of law.

The Supreme Court is also weighing whether to hear a case on bans on AR-15 style rifles. Democrats, now preparing to take control of the Senate, have signaled they could reshape how Trump's judicial and other nominations proceed.

stories.headline: Update: Krakow Gunman Who Killed 6 Has Far-Right Views, Polish Authorities Say
stories.summary:
A 25-year-old Polish man drove into Krakow's Main Square on Saturday and opened fire with an automatic weapon, killing six people and injuring 15 others before police shot and wounded him. The square is a major tourist destination in Poland's second-largest city. Armed police responded, and two nearby schools went into lockdown.

Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said the suspect was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held "very radical views," and described him as a likely domestic far-right extremist. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the attack an act of terrorism. The suspect, a Polish citizen, has been arrested.

A previous report noted that three bodies were later found at the attacker's home, and a British citizen is among the dead. The new development is the authorities' identification of the suspect's ideological motivations and his age. The attack has intensified scrutiny of extremism in Poland, where the political climate is already tense amid disputes between the government and President Karol Nawrocki.

Investigators are expected to examine how the suspect obtained an automatic weapon and whether he had contacts with extremist networks. Authorities have not yet released further details on his background or on the condition of all those wounded.

stories.headline: Update: US Military Fires on Cargo Ship in Gulf of Oman Enforcing Iran Blockade
stories.summary:
A U.S. military aircraft fired on and disabled a St. Kitts-flagged commercial cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Saturday, U.S. Central Command said. CENTCOM said the ship's civilian crew ignored repeated warnings and attempted to breach a naval blockade on Iran. The incident marks a new escalation in the ongoing conflict with Iran.

Separately, CENTCOM announced Task Force Iron Gate, a new unit designed to block Iranian ground transit routes, including across the Caspian Sea, used to move advanced weapons, dual-use technologies, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue. The task force will work with other U.S. agencies. U.S. officials did not say whether military action would be used to stop shipments entering Iran by land.

The Associated Press also reported that President Trump said the U.S. has carried out new limited strikes on Iran targeting air defense systems, while Iran's leaders weigh proposals. Iranian state media reported blasts on Qeshm Island and in Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas. Trump launched major combat operations against Iran on Feb. 28.

The conflict has become a political issue at home. Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended the decision to start the war, while some Republicans and Democrats have questioned it after the midterms, and Vice President JD Vance has been reported to be pushing behind the scenes for a ceasefire and nuclear talks.

stories.headline: Strong Earthquake Shakes Central Japan, Injuring at Least 22
stories.summary:
A magnitude 5.7 earthquake, as measured by the Japan Meteorological Agency, struck central Japan at 1:04 a.m. Sunday, injuring at least 22 people, according to local media. The U.S. Geological Survey put the magnitude at 5.5. The quake was centered about 25 miles below the surface in Shizuoka Prefecture.

The strongest shaking was recorded in neighboring Aichi Prefecture, and a wide area was affected, including Hamamatsu, Kyoto, Nara, Gifu and Yamanashi, home to Mount Fuji. Television footage showed shattered store windows and glass on streets, and a bookstore with books thrown from shelves. Some injuries occurred when people fell on stairs while fleeing buildings. The quake was not felt in Tokyo.

The weather agency warned of possible strong quakes in the coming week, especially over the next two to three days, and urged vigilance for mudslides and falling rocks. An agency official, Ayataka Ebita, said no apparent change had been detected on the Nankai Trough plate boundary, where scientists say a megaquake could occur. Shinkansen bullet trains ran at reduced speeds as a precaution.
